claim.why_it_matters: Three separate index entries are merged into one line, so the page numbers read as one run. The index is informative, but a flattened or merged index entry misattributes page references to the wrong headword.

verdict.reasoning: The rendered page (printed page 903, top of the right column) has three index lines: 'Abbreviated combined relation conditions 165', 'Abnormal run unit termination 438, 440', 'ABS function 642'. page-927.md holds them as one line with no '\' hard breaks, so the claim quotes both sources correctly. Every headword and every page number is present, in the original order, and each number still follows its own headword, so no page reference moves to a different headword. The only difference is the missing line breaks between entries. That is a line-wrapping and formatting defect in the informative index, with no change of content or meaning. The claim's statement that the merge 'misattributes page references to the wrong headword' is not borne out.
